patch.value: GH-1607: Provide intent-specific recovery for unsupported block and unblock commands

**Version:** pm 2026.10.26.

**Repro**
```sh
pm block <id> --reason waiting
pm unblock <id> --note ready
```
**Observed:** both exit 2. `block` suggests `github blockers` and `list --status blocked` (read-only surfaces); `unblock` prints generic examples (`activity`, `aggregate`, `assurance`, …). Neither points at the supported local mutation.

**Expected:** intent-specific recovery for these lifecycle verbs, e.g.
```sh
pm update <id> --blocked-by <blocker> --blocked-reason "waiting"
pm update <id> --dep-remove <blocker> --unset blocked_by --unset blocked_reason --unblock-note "ready"
```
or first-class `block`/`unblock` aliases that map to those flags (never auto-executing a guessed mutation).

**Why it matters for agents:** block/unblock are the verbs agents reach for during a work session; today the failed call is followed by a help search and another attempt (~600–750 bytes of unhelpful stderr each). Note that `--unblock-note` alone records a note but does not remove the blocker edge, which is easy to get wrong without a worked example.


Intake boundary: this is a report against published 2026.10.26, not proof of a current-checkout defect. Reproduce in an external sandbox before implementation. Related completed work retains its shipped scope. Proposed examples or categories are not accepted contracts until validated.

Source: https://github.com/unbraind/pm-cli/issues/1607

Derive examples from live update contracts and prove the suggested block and unblock workflows on isolated trackers.; Unblock recovery explains removal of the actual blocker relationship and stale blocker metadata; a note alone is not presented as unblocking.; Refusals preserve the usage exit code, leave data unchanged, identify the intended lifecycle surface, and retain extension-command and ambiguity behavior. Any new alias must have a declared SDK/CLI/MCP contract.
Unsupported lifecycle verbs lead to a correct local mutation recipe with explicit identifiers and blocker-edge cleanup, without automatically executing an inferred mutation.
